item.content:encoded:
December in Nigeria is practically a season of its own.

Group chats are buzzing, flights are being booked, wedding invitations are coming in, an everyone seems to have holiday plans. From concerts, parties, and social gatherings to family reunions and Christmas celebrations, there is always something happening. For many, it is the most anticipated time of the year, a chance to reconnect with loved ones, explore new places, and make the most of the holidays.

For some, it’s the excitement of Detty December in Lagos. For others, it’s finally getting everyone together for Christmas, taking a much-needed break, or planning a getaway after a long year.

With so much happening, one thing deserves a little more attention than it usually gets: where you’ll be staying.

A good hotel can make all the difference to your holiday. Think relaxing mornings, comfortable rooms, good food, a convenient location, exciting experiences nearby, and somewhere to unwind after a long day of activities. After all, where you stay can shape your entire holiday experience.

Whether you’re planning to experience Detty December in Lagos or spend Christmas in Enugu, we’ve put together a guide to some accommodation options and experiences worth considering as you plan your holiday.

Where to Stay in Lagos for Detty December

Anyone who has experienced Lagos in December knows that the city takes the festive season seriously.

Concerts, weddings, parties, restaurant dates, beach outings, family gatherings and the occasional last-minute plan that turns into the highlight of your holiday, there’s always something happening. With so much going on across the city, staying in a convenient
location can save you time and make getting around much easier.

Victoria Island remains one of Lagos’s most popular areas for visitors during the festive season, thanks to its restaurants, entertainment destinations, and proximity to major lifestyl attractions; it’s a top pick for visitors looking for the best of the city in December.

A top hotel choice located in Landmark Lagos, Oniru, Victoria Island would be the Landmark Hotel, which offers an appealing option for visitors looking to enjoy the best of Lagos while having a comfortable place to retreat to at the end of the day.

With ocean and city views, comfortable accommodation and access to the wider Landmark Lagos leisure and lifestyle ecosystem, Landmark Hotel gives guests more than just a place to stay. It puts them close to a range of experiences, dining options and entertainment destinations, making it easier to enjoy the festive season without having to travel too far.

And the best part? There’s plenty to explore! Guests can enjoy dining experiences within the Landmark ecosystem, visit the Landmark Upside Down House, and attend events at POP Landmark, Landmark Center, or simply spend time exploring the recreational attractions available in the area. Families visiting with children can also plan outings to the Landmark Kids Club.

For visitors coming into Lagos for the holidays, having accommodation close to restaurants and recreational activities can make planning and commuting much easier.

Planning a Christmas Getaway in Enugu? Consider a Lakeside Resort

December isn’t only about the parties.

It’s also one of the few times of the year when families get to spend uninterrupted time together, old friends reconnect, and people finally have an excuse to take that holiday they’ve been postponing. For many people from Eastern Nigeria, including those living
abroad, returning home to celebrate Christmas with family and loved ones is a cherished annual tradition.

If you’re planning a festive getaway this December, Enugu is one destination worth considering. Located in southeastern Nigeria, Enugu is the capital of Enugu State and is popularly known as the Coal City, a name rooted in its historic coal-mining industry.

Beyond its history, the city is known for its scenic hills, rich Igbo cultural heritage, traditional cuisine, and vibrant hospitality and entertainment scene. There is also plenty to explore in and around the city. Visitors can enjoy panoramic views from Milliken Hill, discover the picturesque Ngwo Pine Forest and Waterfall, experience the natural beauty of Awhum Waterfall, or explore Nigeria’s cultural heritage at the National Museum of Unity. And for those looking to enjoy the city’s attractions while having a
peaceful place to relax and reconnect with loved ones, a lakeside getaway offers the perfect opportunity to relax, unwind, and reconnect with loved ones. At Landmark Nike Lake Resort, the surroundings are part of the experience.

The resort, which boasts over 200 rooms and 8 villas, is situated along the scenic shores of Nike Lake, offering a peaceful setting with lush greenery, lake views, comfortable accommodation, and recreational activities. It’s the kind of place where a morning can begin with breakfast overlooking the scenery, followed by a boat ride, an afternoon by the pool, or some outdoor adventure.

For guests who enjoy a little adventure during their stay, there’s plenty to keep them entertained. From quad biking and recreational sports to a visit to the first Upside Down House in the Southeast, there’s something different to make the holiday even more memorable.

The resort also offers dining options and spaces suited to gatherings and celebrations, making it an interesting choice for Christmas holidays, family reunions, and group getaways.

For anyone visiting Enugu during the festive season, Landmark Nike Lake Resort offers more than just a place to stay. It’s an opportunity to slow down, enjoy the beauty of Nike Lake, spend quality time with family and friends, and create new memories along the way. And sometimes, that’s exactly what a holiday should be about.

Tips for Choosing the Right Hotel or Resort This December

December gets busy across Nigeria, and the last thing you want is the wrong accommodation. Before you book, here are four tips to help you get your holiday stay right;

1. Choose a Location That Works for Your Itinerary

Consider the places you intend to visit and the activities on your holiday calendar. If you’re attending concerts, events, or spending most of your time around Victoria Island, staying within the area can help you save valuable time navigating Lagos traffic. For a more relaxed holiday, consider a resort that offers accommodation and recreational experiences within the
same location.

2. Consider Who You’re Travelling With
Your ideal accommodation will depend on the kind of trip you’re planning. Families travelling with children may prefer resorts with adjoining rooms, swimming pools, outdoor activities, and family-friendly attractions, while couples or solo travellers might prioritise comfortable rooms, dining experiences, and convenient access to entertainment.

3. Check the Facilities and What’s Included in Your Booking

Before confirming your reservation, take a moment to find out what your accommodation package covers. Check for amenities such as breakfast, Wi-Fi, parking, recreational facilities, and on-site dining. If you’re booking a resort, confirm which activities are
complimentary and which attract additional charges. This will help you plan your budget and avoid unexpected expenses during your stay.

4. Book Early and Confirm Your Reservation Details

Hotels and resorts often experience increased demand during Christmas and New Year celebrations. Booking ahead gives you a better chance of securing your preferred room type and travel dates. Before making payment, confirm the room rates, check-in and check-out times, cancellation policy, and any festive-season offers or restrictions.

Make the Most of Your December Holiday in Nigeria

The festive season may last only a few weeks, but the best experiences have a way of staying with us long after the celebrations end. The spontaneous outings, memorable adventures, family reunions, and places you finally get to explore often become the stories you carry into the new year.

As you prepare for Detty December 2026, give as much thought to your overall holiday experience as you do to the events on your calendar. A well-planned getaway, with comfortable accommodation and exciting things to see and do, can make all the difference.

With Landmark Hotel in Lagos and Landmark Nike Lake Resort in Enugu, you can look forward to great hospitality, memorable leisure experiences, and convenient access to some of the attractions that make both destinations worth visiting.

Explore Landmark Hotel in Lagos and Landmark Nike Lake Resort in Enugu and start planning your December getaway.

item.title: Tochukwu Ekoh: What My Friend’s Passing Taught Me About Kindness
item.dc:creator: Tochukwu Ekoh
item.description:
I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close, or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way. We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after […]

item.content:encoded:
A thoughtful young woman sits in a relaxed pose in a serene bedroom, reflecting peacefully. Photo credit: Alex Green/Pexels.

I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close, or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way. We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely.

We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there.

Then I heard that he passed away.

My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently?

I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance. Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us?

My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me.

Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect?

Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time? What was the reason for that reconnection, and why did it have to end this way?

The timing of certain events leaves you with more questions than answers.

What makes this loss even more difficult to comprehend is how it happened. I had been the one who suffered an accident, yet I survived and was gradually recovering. He wasn’t sick. He hadn’t been involved in an accident. He simply slipped and fell, sustained an injury, and bled out. His body was not discovered until three days later.

Three days.

The loneliness he must have experienced within those three days, the possibility that he needed someone, and the heartbreaking thought that nobody knew what had happened to him. I cannot fully comprehend it.

It also made me confront something I had perhaps never thought about deeply enough: loneliness. The loneliness that makes you wonder whether anyone would notice if you were suddenly gone. I don’t want to be alone when I pass away.

A week after his burial, I found myself searching his name on Google. I’m not sure what I was looking for. Perhaps I wanted something that would help me process what had happened, something that would make his death feel a little more real or give me some sense of closure. When I read the tributes people had written about him, I began questioning myself. Was I truly kind to this person? Did I appreciate the little things he did? Could I have been more present?

I know I cannot change what happened, and I also know that I cannot take responsibility for circumstances beyond my control. But his death has made me reflect deeply on the kind of person I am and how I want to relate to the people around me.

We do not have to be romantically involved with everyone who cares about us. We do not have to become best friends with everyone we meet. But we can be kind. We can listen. We can check in. We can make a phone call, send a message or simply ask someone how they are doing and genuinely care about the answer.

I am still trying to make sense of his death. I still have questions, and I may never find answers to all of them. I may never understand why our paths crossed again when they did, or why our reconnection had to be so brief. But I know that I do not want this experience to become just another sad memory that eventually fades.

I want it to change something in me. I want to be more intentional about the people around me. I want to check on people, make those calls, offer a listening ear and express love without waiting for a special occasion. I want the goodness of God to be evident not just in what I say, but in how I treat the people I encounter every day.

Because one day, a seemingly ordinary encounter could become our last encounter with someone. When that day comes, I hope the people we leave behind will remember that we made them feel seen, valued and loved.

item.content:encoded:
Entertainment Week Africa (EWA), the pan-African platform for the business of creativity, opens its fifth edition in Lagos tomorrow, Wednesday, 18 November. The programme runs until Saturday, 21 November, and brings together creators, executives, investors, policymakers and delegations from more than 18 African countries.

This year’s theme, Five Years of Closing the Gap, reflects the purpose EWA was built around: connecting African talent with the capital, markets, skills and audiences it needs to grow. Since its first edition, EWA has welcomed more than 67,800 attendees. The 2025 edition alone recorded 28,683 pass-holders from over eight countries and 50 industries, across 61 sessions, 93 film screenings, 20 music showcases and nine fashion showcases.

By day and by night

The week runs across two venues. By day, EbonyLife Place on Victoria Island hosts panels, roundtables, workshops, masterclasses, and film screenings. By night, the programme moves to the Livespot Entertarium in Ikate, beginning with Opening Night on 18 November at 6pm, an evening of music, fashion, film, comedy and awards.

The Entertarium also houses the week’s experiences, including an exhibition, the EWA Art Floor, a fashion show, comedy, live music, a beauty exhibition and a marketplace.

Seven tracks, one market

The 2026 programme is organised across seven tracks: Film & TV; Music; Fashion & Beauty; AI & Tech; Live Events & Production; Creative Enterprise; and Art & Animation, which is new this year.

Alongside the conference, EWA runs a set of commercial formats designed to move deals forward. They include the EWA Deal Room, the Content and Music Markets, the EWA Capital Desk, the Creators Hub and LABSPOT, EWA’s skills and enterprise development engine. Last year’s Deal Room received more than 178 entries and advanced nine companies to its accelerator, with Future Africa, Catalyst Fund, Consonance Invest and Askya Investment Partners among the participating investors and partners.
Between 30 and 40 per cent of this year’s delegates are expected to travel from outside Nigeria, with delegations from Kenya, Rwanda, Ghana, Senegal, Uganda, Tanzania and South Africa among them.

The edition will also host the exclusive screening of University of Side Hustle, the first scripted feature film from Livespot Studios, written by Dami Elebe, executive produced by Deola Art Alade.

The road to Lagos

The fifth edition follows a year in which EWA took its conversation abroad through EWA Creative Connect, its invitation-only convenings. The first was held in Los Angeles during Grammy Week, with executives from Warner Records, Adobe, Amazon and Unilever among the participants. The second took place in London during the Nigeria–UK state visit, with the British Film Institute, Diageo and the Ministry of Trade and Investment in attendance. The third, in Lagos on 12 November, was hosted by U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth.

What The Founders Say

“African creativity deserves stronger platforms, better access and greater value,” said Deola Art Alade, Convener of Entertainment Week Africa and Group CEO of Livespot. “EWA 2026 is our boldest expression of that mission.”

Darey Art Alade, Co-Founder and Chief Creative Officer of Livespot, said: “The next generation of African creative talent needs access, learning, platforms and community. EWA 2026 is about building those bridges with intention.”

Attending

Passes for the Day Sessions and Opening Night are available on DOT Tix at tix.dot360.co. The full schedule is available at ewafrica.com. Follow @ewafrica_ on Instagram for updates throughout the week.

About Entertainment Week Africa

Entertainment Week Africa (EWA) is a pan-African platform for the creative economy, bringing together the people who make, fund and grow Africa’s creative industries across film, music, fashion, technology, art and live entertainment. EWA is an initiative of Livespot Foundation and is produced by Livespot.

item.content:encoded:
• Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management.
  • 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management.
  • Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time.

Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its  Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management.

The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running.

The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform.

The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth.

At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business.

Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time.

Andrew Uaboi, Vice President/Cluster Head Visa West Africa said,


“Digital payments are now a core part of how many SMEs in Nigeria operate. The next opportunity lies in helping businesses get more value from those transactions by connecting payments with the tools they use to manage their day-to-day operations. When payments and business management come together, financial institutions can gain deeper insights into cash flow patterns, support better decision-making, and unlock opportunities to offer more relevant products and services, including access to financing. At Visa, we remain committed to enabling our partners with secure, innovative solutions that help SMEs operate more efficiently and grow with confidence.”

Abiodun Olubitan, Group Head SME Banking at Access Bank added

“For Nigerian SMEs, the opportunity is no longer just about adopting digital payments, but about using digital solutions to run their businesses more efficiently, make informed decisions and unlock new opportunities for growth. At Access Bank, we recognize that when payments are connected to everyday business operations, SMEs can gain better visibility into their cash flow, strengthen financial management and build a stronger foundation for accessing financing. We remain committed to supporting businesses with relevant financial solutions and digital capabilities that help them navigate challenges, scale sustainably and contribute more meaningfully to Nigeria’s economic development.”

About the Study

The Visa Pay and Get Paid 2026 study explores how SMES manage payments, day-to-day operations, and demand for integrated payment and business solutions. The research was conducted through face-to-face interviews with business owners and financial decision-makers between March and April 2026 across 11 markets, including Nigeria, where 251 SMEs were surveyed.

About Visa 

Visa (NYSE: V) is a world leader in digital payments, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories. Our mission is to connect the world through the most innovative, convenient, reliable and secure payments network, enabling individuals, businesses and economies to thrive. We believe that economies that include everyone everywhere, uplift everyone everywhere and see access as foundational to the future of money movement. Learn more at Visa.com.

item.title: Fela Anikulapo-Kuti and Sade Adu Make History With 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Inductions
item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com

Afrobeat pioneer Fela Kuti—represented by Yeni, Femi, Seun, Shalewa, and Made Kuti—and Nigerian-British singer Sade Adu enter the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, with Fela becoming the first African-born solo inductee.

The post Fela Anikulapo-Kuti and Sade Adu Make History With 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Inductions appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today!.
item.content:encoded:
Sade Adu in the Performer category and Fela Kuti in the Early Influence category, both inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Class of 2026.

Nigerian music history just added another major chapter in Los Angeles, and the celebration has been loud from Lagos to London. On Saturday, 14 November 2026, Afrobeat pioneer Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti and Nigerian-British singer Sade Adu were officially inducted into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame during a star-studded ceremony at the Peacock Theatre.

For Fela Kuti, nearly three decades after his passing in 1997, this induction makes him the first African-born solo artist to enter the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Honoured posthumously in the Early Influence category—five years after he was first nominated in 2021—the recognition celebrates how he fused West African rhythms with jazz, funk, and soul to create Afrobeat, using his voice and horns to confront social and political injustice across classics like “Zombie”, “Water No Get Enemy”, and “Sorrow, Tears and Blood”. It also caps off an extraordinary 2026 for his legacy, coming just months after the Recording Academy presented him with a posthumous Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in February, another first for an African artist.

From left, Made Kuti, Femi Kuti, Yeni Kuti, and Seun Kuti in Los Angeles for Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti’s posthumous induction into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Photo Credit: Femi Kuti/Instagram 

Representing the Afrobeat legend on the night were members of the Kuti family, with his children Yeni Kuti, Femi Kuti, Seun Kuti, and Shalewa Kuti, alongside his grandson Made Kuti, stepping out in Los Angeles to accept the honour on his behalf. Speaking on the milestone, the family reflected on how remarkable it is to see Fela receive both the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award and a Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction in the very same year.

Meanwhile, Sade Adu—born Helen Folasade Adu in Ibadan—was inducted in the Performer category as the frontwoman of her acclaimed British band Sade, alongside longtime bandmates Stuart Matthewman, Paul Spencer Denman, and Andrew Hale. Earning their spot on their second nomination, the group behind timeless soul-jazz records such as “Smooth Operator”, “The Sweetest Taboo”, and “Your Love Is King” opted to sit out the ceremony in true low-key fashion, though they shared a warm message thanking fans and dedicating the milestone to their late longtime producer Mike Pela.

From left, Seun Kuti, Yeni Kuti, Femi Kuti, Shalewa Kuti, and Made Kuti arrive on the red carpet at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles for Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti’s posthumous induction into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Photo Credit: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame/Instagram

The 2026 induction class also welcomed a wide range of global icons across its categories, including Phil Collins, Billy Idol, Wu-Tang Clan, Luther Vandross, Oasis, Iron Maiden, and Joy Division/New Order in the Performer category, alongside fellow Early Influence honourees Queen Latifah, MC Lyte, Celia Cruz, and Gram Parsons, with live tribute performances from Megan Thee Stallion, Remy Ma, Gwen Stefani, and Method Man.

For fans eager to watch the Kuti family accept Fela’s plaque and catch all the tributes from the Peacock Theatre, the recorded 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction special will air on ABC and stream on Disney+ on 9 December 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Linda Ejiofor won Best Actress in a Supporting Role for her performance in Daniel Etim-Effiong’s The Herd at the 2026 Africa Movie Academy Awards (AMAA). Photo Credit: Linda Ejiofor/Instagram 

The 2026 Africa Movie Academy Awards (AMAA) brought together some of the continent’s most exciting film talents, with productions from Kenya, Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire and beyond earning recognition across the categories. Two films, in particular, led the winners’ list: the Kenyan-Nigerian co-production One Woman, One Bra, which claimed Best Film alongside two other awards, and Côte d’Ivoire’s The Color of Exile, which secured four wins, including Best Director and Best Actress in a Leading Role.

Hosted by Benneth Ogbeiwi and Sophy Aiida, the ceremony celebrated filmmakers, actors and other industry talents whose work continues to shape African cinema.

The Kenyan-Nigerian co-production “One Woman, One Bra” emerged as the undisputed titan of the evening. Directed by Vincho Nchogu, the film walked away with the most coveted prizes of the night, securing Best Film, the Ousmane Sembène Award for Best Film in an African Language, and Best Debut Feature Film by a Director. Its triumph follows an impressive run on the international festival circuit, including a selection to represent Kenya at the Academy Awards.

Hot on its heels was Côte d’Ivoire’s “The Color of Exile”, which swept four major categories to claim the title of most-awarded single film at the ceremony. Azlarabe Alaoui took home Best Director, Naky Sy Savane earned Best Actress in a Leading Role, alongside twin technical victories in Achievement in Cinematography and Achievement in Sound.

Nigerian cinema also made its formidable presence felt with a total of eight wins across various categories.”To Adaego With Love” captured the National Film and Video Censors Board (NFVCB) Award for Best Nigerian Film alongside Achievement in Screenplay. Meanwhile, Daniel Etim-Effiong’s “The Herd” turned its nominations into gold with wins for Achievement in Production Design, Achievement in Make-Up, and a stellar win for Linda Ejiofor, who picked up Best Actress in a Supporting Role.

In the acting categories, Wale Ojo delivered a brilliant victory for Nigeria by winning Best Actor in a Leading Role for his performance in “Lights Out.” Over in the regional and diaspora categories, Uganda’s Samuel Kabugo secured Best Actor in a Supporting Role for “Slum Bomber“, while Ghana’s “The Fisherman” claimed Achievement in Costume Design, and Nigeria’s “The Creek” and “Evi” picked up wins for visual effects and soundtrack respectively.

item.content:encoded:
The Journey of Future Awards Winner Nene Joy Ojo and Brila Media’s Commitment to Nigerian Sports

Before the applause and the cash prize presented by Brila Media at The Future Awards Africa 2026, Nene Joy Ojo had already spent years building a name for herself in the boxing ring.

Today, we are proud to congratulate her on emerging as the winner of the Sports Award category at The Future Awards Africa 2026.

Her recognition is a significant moment, but it is also a fitting acknowledgement of the work, discipline, and achievements that have brought her to this stage.

Nene Joy Ojo’s story is one of steady progression and impressive milestones.

She began attracting attention as an amateur boxer, winning the African Youth Games gold medal in 2018. Her performances at home also earned recognition, including being named Best Boxer at the Lagos Monthly Saturday Boxing Show in 2019 and again in 2020.

She continued to represent Nigeria on the continental stage, winning gold in the women’s 57kg category at the 2023 African Games in Accra, Ghana. Her journey also took her to the African Olympic qualification tournament in Dakar, where she reached the semi-finals in the same weight category.

In August 2024, Ojo made the transition to professional boxing. She went on to record three victories in the first six months of her professional career, adding another chapter to an already promising journey.

These achievements speak to more than medals and wins. They reflect years of preparation, resilience, and the determination to keep progressing in a demanding sport.

Her Future Awards Africa recognition, therefore, represents an important milestone in a journey that has been unfolding long before the ceremony.

Why This Recognition Matters to Us

At Brila Media, sports has always been about more than results. It is about the people behind the performances, the journeys that deserve to be heard, and the talent that needs the right platforms to grow.

That is why we were pleased to partner with The Future Awards Africa 2026 in supporting the Sports Award category.

For an organisation that has spent decades telling Nigeria’s sports stories, the partnership was an opportunity to extend that commitment beyond coverage and commentary. We wanted to be part of recognising an athlete whose achievements deserve greater visibility and whose journey can inspire the next generation.

It was a special moment for us to present Nene Joy Ojo with a ₦1 million cash prize at the ceremony. But we also believe that supporting an athlete should not end with the presentation of an award.

Our commitment includes producing a documentary that will tell more of her story and a three-month media support package for a foundation of her choice. Through these initiatives, we hope to contribute to the visibility of her journey and the work she chooses to support.

We see this as part of what media can do: not only report achievement but also help preserve the stories behind it, connect them with wider audiences, and create opportunities for their impact to travel further.

Celebrating the Women Shaping Nigerian Sports

Ojo’s achievement is also part of a wider story we are excited to see unfolding across Nigerian sports.

From boxing to football, athletics, weightlifting, and other disciplines, Nigerian women continue to demonstrate their ability to compete, excel, and make history. Their achievements are challenging old limitations and creating new possibilities for girls who are beginning to imagine themselves in sports.

For us, these stories deserve more than occasional attention. They deserve consistent coverage, recognition, and support.

When a young woman sees someone like Nene Joy Ojo celebrated for her achievements in boxing, it makes the possibility of pursuing that path more visible. Recognition can encourage ambition, but sustained support is what helps talent develop and careers endure.

This is one of the reasons we consider partnerships such as this important.

A Celebration, and a Commitment Beyond the Ceremony

“We congratulate Nene Joy Ojo once again on winning the Sports Award at The Future Awards Africa 2026. We are proud to have presented the award and to be contributing to the next chapter of her story.We also appreciate The Future Awards Africa for providing a platform that recognises young Nigerians making meaningful contributions across different fields.

As Brila Media continues to grow as a multimedia organisation, we remain committed to telling stories that matter, celebrating excellence, and creating more opportunities for the people shaping Nigerian sports.

‘Nene’s journey reminds us that recognition is most meaningful when it acknowledges the work already done and encourages what is still possible.

Congratulations, Nene Joy Ojo. This award celebrates how far you have come, and we look forward to seeing how far your journey will go.

item.content:encoded:
Rocky Dawuni, Angélique Kidjo, and Burna Boy are among the African nominees at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards.

If your timelines have been buzzing with celebration, hot takes, and group-chat debates since the 69th Annual Grammy Awards nominations dropped, you are definitely not alone. From record-breaking milestones to long-awaited solo albums and cross-continental collaborations, African nominees at the 2027 Grammys are having a massive moment across both the global and genre-specific categories—with Nigerian, Ghanaian, and Beninese stars leading the charge.

Leading the headlines is Tems, who has officially made history as a 12-time Grammy nominee and the first Nigerian woman to earn four nominations in a single year. Already a two-time Grammy winner—having picked up Best Melodic Rap Performance in 2023 for her feature on Future’s “Wait for U” alongside Drake, and Best African Music Performance in 2025 for “Love Me JeJe”—she returns to the 69th Grammy Awards in four categories. Her acclaimed project Love Is a Kingdom is up for Best Global Music Album, while “Big Daddy” competes for Best African Music Performance, and “What You Need” earns double recognition in Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song.

Right alongside her in the Best African Music Performance race is an exciting lineup of Nigerian, Ghanaian, and Beninese stars. Asake secures two nods in the category—for his solo song “Gratitude” and for “Jogodo” alongside Wizkid—bringing his career total to four Grammy nominations following his previous nods for “Amapiano” with Olamide in 2024 and “MMS” with Wizkid in 2025. For Wizkid, “Jogodo” marks his seventh career Grammy nomination, adding to a run that includes his 2021 Best Music Video win for “Brown Skin Girl” with Beyoncé, Blue Ivy Carter, and Saint Jhn. Ghanaian musicians King Ayisoba and Rocky Dawuni also join the Best African Music Performance lineup with their nomination for “No Tradition, No Africa”.

Tems, Asake, and Ayra Starr lead the stellar lineup of African nominees contending for Best African Music Performance at the 69th Grammy Awards.

Ayra Starr is celebrating a major milestone of her own, earning two nominations at the 69th Grammy Awards to bring her career total to four nods, following earlier Best African Music Performance recognition for “Rush” in 2024 and “Gimme Dat” in 2026. This cycle, she competes in Best Global Music Album for her album Starrgirl and teams up with five-time Grammy winner Angélique Kidjo in Best African Music Performance for “Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)”. Kidjo picks up three nominations in total this year, adding Best Global Music Album for Hope!! and Best Global Music Performance for “Bando [Orchestral]” featuring Pharrell Williams and Quavo.

Angélique Kidjo and Ayra Starr sitting in a recording studio for their Aye Kan collaboration. Photo Credit: Angélique Kidjo/Instagram

Over in the Best Global Music Album category, Davido joins Tems, Ayra Starr, and Angélique Kidjo with his album Oriadé—meaning African artists claim four of the five spots in the category. This marks Davido’s sixth career Grammy nomination, building on his previous nods across the 66th, 67th, and 68th editions for Timeless, “Feel”, “Unavailable” featuring Musa Keys, “Sensational” with Chris Brown and Lojay, and “With You” featuring Omah Lay. Meanwhile, Burna Boy—who won Best Global Music Album in 2021 for Twice as Tall—extends his record as Nigeria’s most-nominated artist in Grammy history with 14 career nods after earning a nomination in Best Global Music Performance for “Dai Dai”, his collaboration with Colombian superstar Shakira.

Burna Boy and Shakira share a warm embrace backstage following their live performance of the official 2026 FIFA World Cup anthem “Dai Dai”.

Mark your calendars for Sunday, 7 February 2027, when the winners will be announced live at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. The 69th Grammy Awards ceremony will broadcast on ABC and stream live on Disney+ and Hulu starting at 4:00 p.m. PT / 7:00 p.m. ET (1:00 a.m. WAT on Monday, 8 February),following the Premiere Ceremony at the Peacock Theater earlier in the day—so get ready to tune in and see which African stars bring home the gold.

item.content:encoded:
Tems receiving the Best African Music Performance at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards.

In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy‘s Ye, CKay‘s Love Nwantiti, Wizkid‘s explosive Essence, to Rema‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally.

While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album.

Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. A song should not earn a nomination simply because it is popular or has enjoyed international success.

A closer look at the nominations across the four editions reveals just how much Nigerian music has featured in the category. In 2024, four of the five nominated recordings featured Nigerian artists. The following year, all five recordings had Nigerian representation, with seven Nigerian artists making the list. In 2026, three of the five recordings featured Nigerian artists, while the 2027 nominations saw four out of five recordings feature at least one Nigerian artist. Altogether, Nigerian artists have featured in 16 of the 20 nominated recordings since the category was introduced.

This is not to suggest that Nigerian music does not deserve the recognition it receives. Nigerian artists have built impressive international careers, and their music has found audiences far beyond the continent. They deserve to be recognised. However, when a category is created to recognise the best of African music, it is worth asking how much of the continent’s musical diversity is reflected in its nominations.

In September 2024, Tyla made a similar observation when she won the Best Afrobeats award at the MTV Video Music Awards. In her acceptance speech, she said, “There is a tendency to group all African artists under Afrobeats… Even though Afrobeats has run things and has opened so many doors for us, African music is so diverse. It is more than just Afrobeats.” Africa has a vast and diverse music industry. From South Africa’s Amapiano movement and Ghana’s Highlife and Hiplife traditions to Uganda’s dance music, Tanzania’s Bongo Flava and the different sounds emerging from Francophone Africa, there is no shortage of music deserving of international attention.

The prominence of Nigerian artists in this category may partly reflect the strength of the country’s music industry and the international visibility its artists have built over the years. It may also reflect the Recording Academy’s membership, voting processes and the music that reaches its voters. But that is precisely why the conversation is important. If the category is to represent African music, its nominations should encourage listeners to discover artists and sounds beyond the ones they already know.

Nigerian music has benefited from a relatively strong music industry, with established record labels, international distribution deals, collaborations with global artists and a large diaspora audience that continues to support its exports. These factors have helped Nigerian artists reach international audiences and, by extension, become more visible to institutions such as the Recording Academy.

However, this visibility does not necessarily mean that the best or most interesting music coming out of Africa is always the music that gets heard internationally. An artist from another African country may be producing equally compelling music but lack the distribution network, marketing resources or international connections to get it beyond their local market. If the music awards are interested in recognising the best of African music, perhaps there is also a need to look beyond the music that already has an established international audience. After all, one of the things an award can do is introduce the world to music it might otherwise never discover.

There is a difference between recognising the best of African music and repeatedly recognising only the most internationally visible parts of it. The Best African Music Performance has opened an important door for African music. The next step is ensuring that more of the continent gets to walk through it.

item.title: This Week’s Playlist Update Comes With Wande Coal, Seyi Shay, Olamide, Khaid & More
item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.description:
Wande Coal (“Kowope”), Patoranking and Olamide (“Welcome to Lagos”), Khaid and King Dr. Saheed Osupa (“Yasin”), Spyro (“Kpan Kpan”), and Seyi Shay with Vegedream (“Love & War”) deliver five fresh Nigerian releases for the week.

The post This Week’s Playlist Update Comes With Wande Coal, Seyi Shay, Olamide, Khaid & More appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today!.
item.content:encoded:
Seyi Shay teams up with French artist Vegedream on her new single “Love & War”, one of the standout releases in this week’s music roundup. Photo Credit: Instagram

A fresh Monday means it is time to clear out last week’s queue and make room for the sounds shaping Nigerian music right now. From Wande Coal reuniting with Juls and Patoranking linking up with Olamide for a musical salute to Lagos, to Khaid bridging generations with Fuji legend Saheed Osupa, Spyro delivering a quick dancefloor starter, and Seyi Shay trading English and French verses with Vegedream, there is plenty to keep your headphones busy over the next few days.

Wande Coal – “Kowope”

Kicking things off is Wande Coal, who reunites with British-Ghanaian producer Juls on “Kowope”, marking their first collaboration since the hit “So Mi So”. The new single is also Wande Coal’s first solo release since he put out his 15-track album KING COAL in June. This time, the pair lean into warm, percussion-led Afropop, with lyrics centred on wealth,celebration and abundance. Ahead of its release on 12 November 2026, Wande Coal gave fans a taste of what was coming with a video staged as an owambe celebration inside a banking hall—a fitting preview for a song that takes its cues from the festive side of Nigerian life.

Patoranking featuring Olamide – “Welcome to Lagos”

Keeping that celebratory mood going, Patoranking and Olamide join forces on “Welcome to Lagos” to give Nigeria’s commercial capital its own musical tribute. The Afro-dancehall collaboration captures the city’s familiar mix of hustle,nightlife and everyday movement, with both artists bringing their distinct sounds to the record. Patoranking opens with his dancehall delivery, setting the pace before Olamide takes over with Yoruba verses rooted in the city’s street culture.Released on 10 November 2026 alongside an official music video, the track gives two of Nigerian music’s established names a chance to celebrate the city that continues to inspire countless songs.

Khaid featuring King Dr. Saheed Osupa – “Yasin”

Switching lanes from contemporary street anthems to a meeting of two musical eras, Khaid takes an unexpected turn on “Yasin” alongside Fuji veteran King Dr. Saheed Osupa. The song brings Khaid’s contemporary Afrobeats melodies together with Osupa’s traditional Fuji vocals and talking-drum rhythms, giving both artists room to draw on their distinct musical styles. An official lyric video followed on 14 November 2026. With this collaboration, Khaid steps beyond the sound audiences may be most familiar with, while Osupa brings his unmistakable Fuji influence to a new musical setting.

Spyro – “Kpan Kpan”

If you are looking to pick up the tempo even further, Spyro keeps things firmly on the dancefloor with “Kpan Kpan”, a two-minute, 19-second Afropop release produced by Colonel Tyemmy. The track is built around bouncy percussion and a hook that is easy to pick up, making it a straightforward party selection. Released on 13 November 2026, “Kpan Kpan” keeps the arrangement brief and gets straight to its upbeat, dance-ready sound.

Seyi Shay featuring Vegedream – “Love & War”

Slowing things down to close out the week’s roundup, Seyi Shay and French-Ivorian singer Vegedream explore the complicated side of romance on “Love & War”, a bilingual duet shaped like a conversation between two people after a breakup. Produced by Grammy-winning producer Harmony “HMoney” Samuels, the song moves between Seyi Shay’s English verses and Vegedream’s French vocals, with both artists approaching the relationship from their own perspectives. Released on 13 November 2026, the track draws on the familiar saying that all is fair in love and war, using the back-and-forth between its two voices to explore the tension between affection and heartbreak.

item.content:encoded:
Tems is officially a 12-time Grammy nominee after securing four nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards. Photo Credit: Tems/Instagram 

One, two, three… and now 12! Tems has added four more Grammy nominations to her record, bringing her career total to 12 ahead of the 69th Grammy Awards. The latest recognition also makes her the first Nigerian female artist to receive four nominations in a single Grammy year, with this year’s shortlist recognising her work across four categories.

The Nigerian singer is in contention for Best Global Music Album with her 10-track EP, Love Is a Kingdom, and Best African Music Performance for “Big Daddy”. She has also earned nominations for Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song for “What You Need”. The four nominations give her one of the most extensive Nigerian representations at this year’s ceremony and bring her Grammy wins to two, following previous victories in 2023 and 2025.

Her relationship with the Recording Academy began in 2022, when she received her first nomination for her contribution to Wizkid‘s “Essence”, which was nominated for Best Global Music Performance at the 64th Grammy Awards. The following year brought three more nominations, this time for her work on Future’s “Wait for U” featuring Drake and Beyoncé‘s Renaissance. She won her first Grammy that night, taking home Best Melodic Rap Performance for “Wait for U”, while also receiving nominations for Album of the Year and Best Rap Song.

Tems earned another nomination at the 66th Grammy Awards in 2024 for “Lift Me Up”, her contribution to the Black Panther: Wakanda Forever soundtrack, in the Best Song Written for Visual Media category. She returned to the Grammys the following year with three nominations, including Best Global Music Album for her debut album, Born in the Wild, and Best R&B Song for “Burning”. Her second Grammy win came in the Best African Music Performance category, where “Love Me JeJe” took home the award at the 67th Grammy Awards in February 2025.

Now, with four nominations for the 69th edition, Tems has added another significant chapter to her Grammy record. The ceremony will take place on Sunday, 7 February 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.

item.content:encoded:
The Africa Women Innovation and Entrepreneurship Forum (AWIEF) is pleased to announce the winners of its 2026 AWIEF Awards.

Launched in 2017, the prestigious annual AWIEF Awards recognise, honour and celebrate outstanding women entrepreneurs, innovators, and leaders across various industry sectors for their achievements and contributions to Africa’s inclusive economic growth and development.

The 2026 awards ceremony and gala dinner took place on 11 November 2026 at the Cape Town International Convention Centre (CTICC) as part of the AWIEF2026 Conference, which convened over 600 entrepreneurs, business leaders, investors, policymakers, development partners, and key stakeholders from across Africa and beyond.

Following a highly competitive nominations process, this year’s winners represent an inspiring range of industries and African markets, reflecting the breadth of entrepreneurial talent, innovation, and impact across the continent.

The 2026 awards recognised outstanding achievements across seven categories, including emerging entrepreneurial leaders, agricultural innovators, technology pioneers, creative visionaries, and individuals driving meaningful social impact.

The Male Ally Award, introduced in 2026, recognises the important role of men in advancing women’s economic empowerment and championing greater inclusion and gender equality.

The Lifetime Achievement Award honours an exceptional female leader whose decades of leadership, entrepreneurship, and public service have contributed significantly to Africa’s economic, social, and institutional development while paving the way for future generations of women leaders.

WOMAN TO WATCH AWARD

Faith Nafula – Founder & CEO, Solar Spark Energy, Kenya

AGRI AWARD

Joyce Rugano – CEO, Ecorich Solutions, Kenya

IMPACT FOR GOOD AWARD

Echo Nomsa VanderWal – Executive Director, The Luke Commission, Eswatini

CREATIVE VISIONARY AWARD

Renuka Methil – Managing Editor, Forbes Africa, South Africa

TECH PIONEER AWARD

Quinter Ochieng – Founder & CEO, Chargebyte Africa, Kenya

MALE ALLY AWARD

John de Wit – Small Enterprise Foundation (SEF), South Africa

LIFETIME ACHIEVEMENT AWARD

Mary Okelo – P & M Investment, Kenya

Celebrating Excellence and Inspiring the Next Generation

The AWIEF Awards remain an important platform for recognising the individuals shaping Africa’s entrepreneurial and innovation landscape. Beyond celebrating individual achievements, the awards highlight the importance of entrepreneurship, inclusive leadership, innovation, and collaboration in driving sustainable economic growth across the continent.

AWIEF congratulates all the 2026 winners and celebrates their outstanding contributions to Africa’s entrepreneurial ecosystem.

item.content:encoded:
Nigerian music stars Ayra Starr, Davido, and Tems claim three of the five slots in the Best Global Music Album category at the 69th Grammy Awards.

The music industry in Nigeria is in a celebratory mood right now as three Nigerian artists — Davido, Tems, and Ayra Starr — are officially in the running for the prestigious Best Global Music Album award at the 69th Grammy Awards.

Presented annually by the Recording Academy, the Best Global Music Album category honours full-length studio albums and extended plays that celebrate non-Western musical traditions and cross-cultural sounds from around the world. Claiming three out of the five available spots in a single year marks an extraordinary showing for Nigerian music on the international stage.

Marking his sixth career Grammy nod, Davido is nominated for his sixth studio album, Oriadé. Released on 31 July 2026 to commemorate 15 years in the music industry, the 13-track project draws its title from the Yoruba words for destiny (“Ori”) and crown (“Adé”). Across songs featuring Black Sherif, Mayorkun, Fola, Leon Thomas, Aya Nakamura, and Llona, the album reflects on gratitude, ambition, and his musical roots across Afrobeats, R&B, and amapiano. This nod follows three nominations at the 66th Grammys in 2024 (Timeless for Best Global Music Album, “Feel” for Best Global Music Performance, and “Unavailable” featuring Musa Keys for Best African Music Performance), a nomination in 2025 for “Sensational” alongside Chris Brown and Lojay, and a 2026 nod for “With You” featuring Omah Lay.

Tems is also competing for the prize with her seven-track extended play, Love Is a Kingdom, which arrived as a surprise release on 21 November 2025. Built around alternative R&B and Afrobeats rhythms, the project explores romance, self-worth, and spiritual reflection across tracks including “First“, “Big Daddy“, “Lagos Love“, and “What You Need“. Beyond her album recognition, Tems leads the Nigerian contingent at the 69th Grammy Awards with four nominations in total, becoming the first Nigerian female artist to earn four nods in a single year. She is also nominated for Best African Music Performance for “Big Daddy”, as well as Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song for “What You Need”. A two-time Grammy winner, she previously claimed Best Melodic Rap Performance in 2023 for her contribution to Future’s “Wait for U” featuring Drake, and Best African Music Performance in 2025 for “Love Me JeJe“, while her debut album Born in the Wild was nominated in this global album category in 2025.

Rounding out the Nigerian trio is Ayra Starr, who makes her debut appearance in the Best Global Music Album category with her third studio album, Starrgirl. Released on 14 August 2026, the 15-track album captures her growth and confidence across songs such as “Tornado“, “Heaven Baby” featuring Zayn, “Hot Body“, “Who’s Dat Girl” with Rema, and “Gimme Dat” with Wizkid. Ayra Starr picked up a second nomination at the 2027 Grammys in the Best African Music Performance category for “Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)” alongside Beninese music icon Angélique Kidjo. These two nods bring her career tally to four Grammy nominations, following earlier Best African Music Performance recognition for “Rush” in 2024 and “Gimme Dat” in 2026.

Joining the Nigerian stars in representing the African continent is five-time Grammy winner Angélique Kidjo,nominated for her 19th studio album, Hope!!, which was released on 24 April 2026 and features guest appearances from Davido, Ayra Starr, and The Cavemen. Brazilian pop star Anitta completes the five-nominee shortlist with Equilibrivm.

The Recording Academy will announce the winners when the 69th Grammy Awards hold on Sunday, 7 February 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.

item.content:encoded:
Nigeria’s leading event technology company, Mobile Screens and Sound Limited (MSS), has  marked two decades of pioneering innovation, industry transformation and excellence with  a landmark gala held on Thursday, October 8, at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos. 

The event, themed The Art of Experience, brought together an influential gathering of  business leaders, government officials, industry stakeholders, clients, partners and friends  of the brand to celebrate a company whose innovations have helped shape the modern  events landscape in Nigeria. 

For 20 years, MSS has remained at the forefront of event technology, delivering the sound,  visuals, staging and technical expertise behind some of Nigeria’s most significant corporate,  entertainment, government and cultural events. From introducing cutting-edge LED screen  technology at a time when it was largely unfamiliar to the market, to becoming one of the  country’s most trusted providers of integrated event production solutions, MSS has  consistently redefined what is possible in the live experiences industry.

The evening showcased the company’s remarkable journey from a bold entrepreneurial  venture into an industry leader whose footprint extends across every facet of event  technology. Through immersive storytelling, visual displays and experiential installations,  guests were taken through the evolution of MSS and the pivotal role it has played in raising  industry standards and inspiring the growth of an entire ecosystem of event technology  providers. 

Reflecting on the company’s journey, Founder and Managing Director, Tunbosun Kola-Daisi,  said: 

“Twenty years ago, we entered an industry where the solutions we offered were largely  unfamiliar and where belief in the future of event technology was limited. LED screens,  which are commonplace today, were then considered a novelty. The early years tested our  resilience, and it took nearly five years before we broke even. But we remained steadfast in  our vision because we understood the transformative power of technology in creating  unforgettable experiences. 

Today, as we celebrate this milestone, we are proud not only of what we have built, but of  the role MSS has played in shaping an industry, creating opportunities and setting new  standards for excellence.” 

A defining moment of the evening was the unveiling of the company’s new logo and refreshed  brand identity, signalling a bold new chapter in MSS’ evolution. The rebrand reflects the  company’s growth and reinforces its position as a comprehensive provider of event  technology solutions spanning sound, lighting, screens, production services, and immersive  audience experiences. 

The unveiling culminated in a spectacular drone display that illuminated the Lagos skyline,  symbolising the innovation, ambition and creativity that have defined the MSS journey for  two decades. 

Speaking on the company’s future direction, Kola-Daisi added: “What began as a vision to  transform event experiences has evolved into a business capable of powering some of the  largest and most complex productions in Nigeria. Today, we can deliver large-scale sound  reinforcement across major venues, deploy screens simultaneously across multiple events,  support uninterrupted operations through an extensive power infrastructure, execute  nationwide advertising installations, transform physical spaces into immersive experience  centres, and provide end-to-end production management for events of every scale. 

But this is only the beginning. Our next chapter is focused on deeper innovation, strategic  expansion across Africa and investing in the people who will drive the future of this industry. 

We are committed to remaining the benchmark for event technology excellence while  building the next generation of industry professionals.” 

The anniversary celebration also highlighted MSS’ commitment to developing talent through  the recently launched MSS Event Tech Academy, a pioneering capacity-building initiative  designed to address the growing demand for skilled professionals within the event  technology ecosystem. Delivered in partnership with KolaDaisi University, the intensive 10- week programme provided participants with both technical and practical training across six  specialist areas: LED Screen Engineering, Sound Engineering, Camera Craft and Video  Production, Lighting Design and Control, Event Management and Production, and Rigging  and Trussing. 

More than 60 students completed the inaugural programme, gaining valuable hands-on  experience through participation in live MSS projects and productions. Demonstrating the  academy’s tangible impact, five graduates secured immediate employment with MSS upon completion of the programme. 

As Nigeria’s event technology industry continues to evolve, MSS remains committed to  advancing professional standards, nurturing talent and driving innovation that elevates live  experiences across the continent. Twenty years after helping pioneer a new era of event  technology in Nigeria, MSS continues to set the pace, proving that exceptional experiences  are not merely produced, but carefully engineered. 

About Mobile Screens and Sound Limited (MSS) 

Mobile Screens and Sound Limited (MSS) is Nigeria’s leading event technology company,  delivering world-class solutions across sound, lighting, LED displays, staging, live production  and experiential event management. With two decades of industry leadership, MSS has  powered some of the country’s most notable live, corporate and entertainment events while  championing innovation, professional excellence and talent development within the event  technology sector.

item.content:encoded:
Lagos has no shortage of events, but from 19 to 21 November, The Glenlivet is planning something a little different. 

For three nights, Lagos will host The Glenlivet Experience, a curated immersion into the heritage, craftsmanship and distinctive character of the iconic Speyside single malt Scotch whisky, brought to life through a distinctly Lagos lens.

Across the three days, The Glenlivet’s Brand Ambassadors, Ebuka Obi-Uchendu, Osas Ighodaro and Farooq Oreagba, will join the brand’s Tastemakers and guests from across culture, business, fashion, music and hospitality.

Evane Chenuet, Marketing Director, Pernod Ricard Nigeria, said:

“We wanted people to experience The Glenlivet single malt whisky rather than simply hear about it. The Glenlivet Experience brings our rich brand’s heritage to life in a way that feels contemporary, culturally relevant and that immerses our guests in our spirit of originality .” 

The first two days will welcome a curated audience, while on 21st November, the Experience will extend its invitation to a wider community, offering more guests the opportunity to discover the world of The Glenlivet.

The Glenlivet Experience
 19–21 November 2026
 5:00 PM – 11:00 PM

For updates on registration and access, follow @TheGlenlivetNG on Instagram.

item.title: Asake, Tems, Wizkid & Ayra Starr Lead African Acts Nominated for 2027 Grammys
item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.description:
Asake earns two nominations in the Best African Music Performance category at the 69th Grammy Awards, alongside Wizkid, Tems and Ayra Starr. Ghanaian musicians King Ayisoba and Rocky Dawuni also receive a nomination.

The post Asake, Tems, Wizkid & Ayra Starr Lead African Acts Nominated for 2027 Grammys appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today!.
item.content:encoded:
Tems, Asake, and Ayra Starr lead the stellar lineup of African nominees contending for Best African Music Performance at the 69th Grammy Awards.

The Recording Academy has just rolled out the official nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards, and the Best African Music Performance category is an absolute powerhouse lineup with Nigerian artists making up a significant part of this year’s shortlist.

Leading the category is Asake, who pulled off an incredible double entry in the category. He picked up a solo nod for his standout track “Gratitude” alongside a stellar collaborative nomination for “Jogodo” alongside Wizkid. For Wizkid, this latest nomination adds another major chapter to his historic Grammy legacy, building on his previous career milestones, which include his historic win for Best Music Video with Beyoncé for “Brown Skin Girl” at the 63rd Grammy Awards in 2021, as well as multiple past nominations.

Tems is another Nigerian nominee, returning to the category she won at the 67th Grammy Awards in February 2025 with “Love Me JeJe”. This time, she is nominated for “Big Daddy”. Her previous Grammy win came in 2023, when she received Best Melodic Rap Performance for her contribution to Future‘s “Wait for U”, featuring Drake.

The Nigerian representation also includes Ayra Starr, whose nomination comes through “Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)”, a collaboration with Beninese music legend Angélique Kidjo. Ayra Starr previously received a nomination in the category for “Rush”, while Angélique Kidjo brings her own Grammy-winning history to the collaboration, with wins for albums including Eve, Sings, Celia and Mother Nature.

Rounding out the category with rich cultural resonance are Ghanaian musicians King Ayisoba and Rocky Dawuni, who earned a brilliant nomination for “No Tradition, No Africa“.

The 69th Grammy Awards will hold on 7 February 2027 at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.

item.content:encoded:
Nigerian actress, trained lawyer, and TFAA co-host Genoveva Umeh dressed for the 20th edition of The Future Awards Africa. Photo Credit: The Future Awards Africa/Instagram

A historic hosting line-up spanning five African countries and the introduction of a first-of-its-kind AI assistant named Infinity marked the 20th edition of The Future Awards Africa (TFAA), held on Saturday, 14 November 2026, at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos.

Themed “Celebrating The Redefiners: Africa’s AI Generation,” the ceremony recognised young Africans aged 18 to 35 across 26 categories, including technology and innovation, entrepreneurship, governance, music, film, literature, advocacy, sports and fashion.

The anniversary edition was hosted by five personalities from across the continent: Nigerian actress and trained lawyer Genoveva Umeh; Kenyan media personality Claudia Naisabwa; Malawian radio broadcaster and television personality Priscilla Kayira; Botswana television and radio host Resego Motlhokathari; and Tanzanian actor and former Big Brother Africa winner Idris Sultan.

Co-hosts Genoveva Umeh, Resego Motlhokathari, Claudia Naisabwa, Idris Sultan, and Priscilla Kayira pose together ahead of the 20th anniversary ceremony. Photo Credit: The Future Awards Africa/Instagram

They shared the stage with Infinity, an AI assistant that interacted with the hosts through quick-witted and playful responses, drawing laughter from guests throughout the ceremony. Its introduction brought artificial intelligence into the evening’s entertainment, while musical performances by Sharp Band and the Loud Urban Choir added to the celebrations.

Among the evening’s major winners, Nora Awolowo received the Prize for Young Person of the Year, Teniola Aladese won the Prize for Acting, and Olamidun Ogundoyin took home the Prize for Entrepreneurship. Pastor Jerry Uchechukwu Eze, represented at the ceremony by media personality Hero Daniels, received the Prize for Service to Young People.

The ceremony also welcomed representatives of distinguished public figures, including Mobolaji Abubakre Ogunlende, Lagos State Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, who represented Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu.

Another highlight was the recognition of the first winners of The Future Awards Africa Independent (TFAAi), a state-level initiative established in 2026 to spotlight young changemakers whose contributions may receive limited attention on national platforms. Its first edition covered Rivers, Abia, Oyo and Kano States, extending the awards’ reach into more communities.

Daniel Ekpe (Awkaman) accepts his award on stage at the 20th anniversary edition of The Future Awards Africa. Photo Credit: Daniel Ekpe/Instagram

Reflecting on the milestone, Ayodeji Razaq, Executive Director of The Future Awards Africa, said the 20th edition represented a sustained commitment to recognising young Africans shaping the continent’s future. He also highlighted TFAAi as part of the platform’s effort to ensure exceptional work receives recognition wherever it happens.

TFAA co-founders Chude Jideonwo and Adebola Williams also reflected on the platform’s journey and the generations of young achievers whose stories have shaped its history.

Twenty editions on, The Future Awards Africa continues to recognise young Africans making significant contributions across different fields, while creating room for new voices and achievements across the continent.

item.title: Tiyani Makamu Wins Miss South Africa 2026!
item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.description:
27-year-old entrepreneur and Hubsela founder Tiyani Makamu has been crowned Miss South Africa 2026 in Johannesburg, succeeding Qhawekazi Mazaleni.

The post Tiyani Makamu Wins Miss South Africa 2026! appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today!.
item.content:encoded:
Tiyani Makamu celebrates on stage moments after being crowned Miss South Africa 2026 at the Sandton Convention Centre in Johannesburg on 14 November 2026. Photo Credit: Miss South Africa/Instagram

South Africa has a new queen, and her name is Tiyani Makamu! At a stylish finale held at the Sandton Convention Centre in Johannesburg on Saturday, 14 November 2026, the 27-year-old entrepreneur and youth advocate from Bronkhorstspruit, Gauteng stepped forward to claim the Miss South Africa 2026 crown. Outgoing titleholder Qhawekazi Mazaleni handed over the reins, while Cwenga Koyana Kotu-Rammopo from Edenvale and Lesego Khumo Nyathela from Springs took home the First Princess and Second Princess titles.

Away from the pageant stage, Tiyani Makamu already wears plenty of impressive hats. A graduate of the Pearson Institute of Higher Education, she works as a communications professional, Group Digital Lead, and Client Success Executive, and also runs Hubsela—a small-business support platform she founded to help fellow entrepreneurs build thriving ventures. Her passion for youth employment and business education also shows up in her community work, including supporting a local library initiative in Ivory Park to help young people gain practical skills.

Miss South Africa 2026 Tiyani Makamu, entrepreneur and founder of Hubsela from Bronkhorstspruit, Gauteng. Photo Credit: Miss South Africa/Instagram

What makes Tiyani Makamu’s reign especially exciting is how different Miss South Africa 2026 looks this year. Under the Motsepe Group of Companies’ ownership, the Miss South Africa Organisation shifted its focus toward homegrown leadership and social impact—meaning neither Makamu nor her runners-up will head off to international competitions like Miss Universe, Miss World, or Miss Supranational. Instead, she gets to pour her entire year into community projects across South Africa through the pageant’s Empower Youth Africa initiative, backed by a R1 million cash prize and access to up to R500,000 from the Impact Fund.

Chatting shortly after her crowning at the Sandton Convention Centre—which hosted the finale for the first time after four years in Pretoria—Miss South Africa 2026 Tiyani Makamu shared what she hopes to accomplish over the next twelve months:

My mandate as Miss South Africa is to empower women entrepreneurs by bridging the gaps in access to opportunities, business development and funding. I want to equip women with the skills, resources and financial readiness to build sustainable, thriving businesses. Through entrepreneurship and skills development, I aim to champion the economic empowerment of women and youth across Africa.

Miss South Africa 2026 Tiyani Makamu, who will dedicate her reign to domestic entrepreneurship and youth empowerment across South Africa. Photo Credit: Tiyani Makamu/Instagram

item.title: Here Are Six Simple Ways to Prepare for the New Year
item.dc:creator: Ahmad Adedimeji Amobi
item.description:

item.content:encoded:
In less than 50 days, 2026 will be over. In January, a new year and Christmas that seemed like a long time away are now around the corner. Once Christmas is over, everyone begins to prepare for the new year and write down things they hope to achieve in 2027. As there will be people moving on to new adventures, getting married, moving homes and countries, starting a new job, there will be people who arrive in the new year with no fully shaped plan. Essentially, it is not because they are clueless or fail to prepare for new adventures; sometimes you just don’t have plans. You just don’t know what to expect in the coming year.

As it is popularly known, “He who fails to prepare, prepares to fail.” That only works in schools where, when you don’t prepare for examinations, you might fail. In life, the logic might not exactly apply. You can prepare and still fail; you might not prepare at all and still win.

Yet, it is still important to prepare, just for the sake of it; just because you can and you should. Now, preparation in this context is not a grand master plan. It is not some motivational kit that will prepare you for success in 2027. The preparation here is the simple things that you can do to be ready for a new year. Sometimes, 9-5 workers have no idea what they’ll do at work, but they sure know they have to get ready and prepare for work. Even na just one email dem go send throughout the day, they have to prepare for work. That could be applied here too.

What are the simple ways you can prepare for the new year?

Clean your house

Whether you live alone or still at your parents’, you never know how cleaning and rearranging your house can prepare you for the coming year. Even if you sweep your house daily, rearranging your furniture, moving things around, and changing the general look of your house can build emotional preparation. It also gives your house a different look, unfamiliar to what you’re familiar with. Human beings evolve, and while the phrase “new year, new me” always sounds cliché, it can be true. We are not who we were many years ago.

Also, whether you work from home or in an office, give your working environment a little attention.

Reconnect with people

Adulthood is a full-time job folded into other full-time jobs. We get so caught up in its web and cycle that we forget to check on people important to us. December is the best time to reconnect with people adulthood might have kept you from properly connecting with. Call your friends. Call your family members. Arrange a visit or have a proper conversation with an old friend. Call people for the sake of calling.

Review your finances and your year

Money is important. The amount of money one has in the bank account at the end of the year can define how big one dreams or expects the coming year to be. As the year winds down, it is the best time to reflect on how the year has been personally, professionally and financially.  Check your subscriptions. Cancel services you no longer use.

Make a list of things you enjoyed this year. Not just achievements, but experiences, people, books, places and little moments that made you happy. Reflect on the moments from the year, good and bad, your wins, your losses, big or small, your earnings and expenditure and the consequences of your decisions. These reflections will prepare you for the new year.

Settle outstanding responsibilities

Think about the little things you’ve been postponing. Perhaps you need to renew an important document, address a health issue, fix a leaking tap, update your CV, return something you borrowed or finally resolve an issue you’ve been avoiding. This is for me as much as it is for you. You don’t have to enter January with every problem solved, but attending to some of these things can make the transition into a new year easier.

Clear out your wardrobe

You probably have clothes you haven’t worn in two years, shoes you no longer like and bags that have been hung for many years. This is a good time to sort through them. Give away clothes that are still in good condition but no longer fit you, repair the ones that need fixing and identify those you genuinely need. Decluttering the wardrobe is like letting no longer needs to be in your life, what you need to shed off as you emerge into a new year.

Most importantly, rest

Take a break. Sleep. Spend time with people you love. Watch your favourite films. Allow yourself to do absolutely nothing for a while. You don’t want to enter January already exhausted from trying to make December count. You sef don try.

item.title: Wunmi Adelusi: Why Are We Still Hiding That We Use AI?
item.dc:creator: Wunmi Adelusi
item.description:
